_comment: The demo's pull-request world, authored in the SAME shape the production
PR cache stores (see PrCacheCodec.*ToCache). The seeder writes these rows
verbatim into the `caches` table and DemoPrReviewRepository decodes them
with the real *FromCache functions — so a fixture is a realistic cache
entry rather than a parallel invention.
avatar_url is deliberately EMPTY everywhere: a demo container makes no
outbound request, the media proxy is disabled, and the client renders
initials when there is no avatar. A remote URL here would be the one
thing that broke the zero-egress guarantee.

detail.title: Surface contingency deadlines on the escrow timeline
detail.body:
Contingency deadlines are typed in as fixed calendar dates after acceptance, so they drift every time a window is renegotiated and nothing agrees with the contract.

This derives each deadline from contract acceptance instead — per-contingency business-day windows (inspection 10, financing 21, title 14) behind an `EscrowClock` — and surfaces days-remaining on the closing timeline.

- [x] `EscrowClock` abstraction
- [x] Business-day windows for inspection, financing, title
- [x] Days-remaining on the timeline
- [ ] Decide what happens when two closings share one acceptance date

files.patch:
@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@
 # Changelog
 
-## Unreleased
+## Unreleased
+- Contingency deadlines are derived from acceptance in business days (inspection 10, financing 21, title 14).

commits.message: Derive deadlines from acceptance in business days
Pin the inspection and title windows in tests

reviews.body:
Reviewed 3 files (+118/−26).

**What this does.** Contingency deadlines stop being dates someone types in after acceptance: `deadlineFor` now derives each one from contract acceptance through `EscrowClock` — inspection 10, financing 21, title 14 business days — and `daysRemaining` reads through the same clock, so the timeline, the closing export and the tests share one definition of a business day. Deriving instead of storing also means a renegotiated window needs no migration. That part is correct and I have no notes on it.

**Blocking (1).** The calculation is keyed on the acceptance date alone. Two closings can share one — a re-trade re-accepted the same day, a double escrow on adjacent parcels — and `lib/escrow/extensions.dart:71` recomputes through this same path after an extension is recorded, so one closing's extension shifts the *other* file's inspection, financing and title deadlines everywhere they render. This is the open question in the PR body and it is still unresolved: the calculator needs the closing id (or the acceptance event) in the key.

**Nits (3).**
- `bd` / `bdBetween` on `EscrowClock`, and `_win` here — the most-scrutinized math in the PR under the least searchable names in the codebase. `addBusinessDays`, `businessDaysBetween`, `windowFor` say what they do.
- Inspection (10) and title (14) each have a pinning test; financing (21) is the one window with a legal consequence when it slips, and it has none.
- The clock skips weekends but has no holiday table, so a deadline can land on July 4th and nothing moves it. Fine if deliberate — say so where the windows are declared, because the county recorder does not record that day either.

Approving once the shared-acceptance race is addressed — the rest looks correct.

review_comments.body:
Two closings can share an acceptance date — a re-trade re-accepted the same day, or a double escrow on adjacent parcels. `deadlineFor` resolves from the date alone, so once an extension is recorded on one file, the other closing's inspection, financing and title deadlines shift too. I think this is the "deadlines moved on their own" report.

Could the calculator take the closing id and resolve the window per closing, so an extension on one never moves the other?
Good catch — I'll key the calculator by the acceptance event so each closing resolves its own windows. In this PR, not a follow-up.

issue_comments.body: Rendering note while it's fresh: once a contingency passes its deadline, "0 days remaining" reads like it is still live. Show expired ones as "Expired 2d ago" in the danger tone and stop counting down — otherwise we teach agents to ignore the chip. Mock is in the chip spec if you want it.

detail.title: Add a distinct notarization-pending state to document uploads
detail.body:
Inspection PDFs and disclosure packets upload to 100% and then sit silent while the server-side notarization check runs — on a 1GB scan that is ~30s of nothing, and support logs show people cancel and re-upload a packet that was fine.

This adds a `notarizing` phase between transfer and done so the tile says what is actually happening instead of parking at 99%.

Fixes PD-118.

commits.message: Add an explicit notarizing phase to uploads
Render notarization pending in the tile

reviews.body:
Approved on the state machine — `notarizing` as a real phase instead of a fake 99% is the right call, and the copy matches what we agreed with title ops.

One thing before merge: the ordering failure Diego flagged is real. `UploadPhase.done` is emitted before `_progress.add(1.0)`, so a listener that reads both briefly sees a finished upload at 99%. Flip those two lines and this is mergeable.
